Generated code compilation/loading error:
cuModuleLoadDataEx failed: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_PTX: a PTX JIT compilation failed
PTX JIT error log:
ptxas application ptx input, line 31; error   : Unknown video selector: '.x'
ptxas application ptx input, line 31; error   : Video selector is not allowed on source operand for instruction 'mov'
ptxas application ptx input, line 33; error   : Unknown video selector: '.x'
ptxas application ptx input, line 33; error   : Video selector is not allowed on source operand for instruction 'mov'
ptxas fatal   : Ptx assembly aborted due to errors
Loading ModelNew failed: ModelNew is None
fix:
<reasoning>
Root cause: virtual registers named %tid and %ctaid shadow PTX special registers. When you use %tid.x and %ctaid.x, ptxas treats ".x" as a (illegal) video/vector selector on your scalar registers, causing the PTX JIT error.

Fix: Rename your virtual registers to avoid collisions and read the special registers into them. Specifically:
- Change the .reg declaration to use %g_tid, %g_bdim, %g_cta instead of %tid, %bdim, %ctaid.
- Update the moves from special registers to:
  mov.u32 %g_tid,  %tid.x;
  mov.u32 %g_bdim, %ntid.x;
  mov.u32 %g_cta,  %ctaid.x;
  mad.lo.u32 %g_tid, %g_cta, %g_bdim, %g_tid;
- Replace subsequent uses of %tid with %g_tid.

This preserves the kernel’s behavior and Python glue while eliminating the PTX name collision.
</reasoning>
```json
[
  {
    "action": "replace",
    "line_number": 21,
    "new_code": "    .reg .u32   %g_tid, %g_bdim, %g_cta, %lane, %total;"
  },
  {
    "action": "replace",
    "line_number": 35,
    "num_lines": 4,
    "new_code": [
      "    mov.u32 %g_tid,  %tid.x;",
      "    mov.u32 %g_bdim, %ntid.x;",
      "    mov.u32 %g_cta,  %ctaid.x;",
      "    mad.lo.u32 %g_tid, %g_cta, %g_bdim, %g_tid;"
    ]
  },
  {
    "action": "replace",
    "line_number": 41,
    "new_code": "    setp.ge.u32 %p0, %g_tid, %total;"
  },
  {
    "action": "replace",
    "line_number": 45,
    "new_code": "    mov.u32 %t, %g_tid;"
  }
]
```
